speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On 21 July 2023, last year, a police officer, the late Sgt Uvaraja, committed suicide.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I asked the Police to investigate the allegations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Safety and security in Singapore are based on, among other things, very high levels of public trust and confidence in the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In this matter, allegations were made against the Police by a Police officer.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If there is wrongdoing, it must be dealt with, and it will be dealt with and errant officers must be taken to task.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If we do not do so over time, the public will lose trust in the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: However, if the allegations are unfounded, the facts have to be set out and we will defend the Police publicly and robustly.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If that is not done and untruths are allowed to fester, morale in the Singapore Police Force (SPF) will go down, and public trust will be eroded.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have seen this, and many other things, happen – in the United States (US), the United Kingdom (UK) and many other countries over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Public trust in these police forces has been affected and the morale of their officers has suffered.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And we do not want to go down that path.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, I directed the SPF to investigate the claims and for the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) to review the findings of the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And I am setting them out publicly here.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will deal with four aspects in this Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, I will deal with the allegations and the findings in respect of these allegations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Second, I will set out how the Police had supported Uvaraja.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Third, I will touch on the framework in SPF to deal with workplace harassment and grievances.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And fourth, I will address the mental health support that is provided to Home Team officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have asked my colleagues, Ministers of State Sun Xueling and Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim, to also deliver further Ministerial Statements on my behalf in Mandarin and Malay.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: All the allegations concerning Uvaraja, including those shared by officers who had already left the Force, were looked into.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Out of respect for Uvaraja’s memory and in consideration for his family, I would have preferred not to go into the details of these findings.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But for the reasons I mentioned earlier, we have no choice but to set out at least some of the facts.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, I go into the facts with some regret.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They have been told in detail what I am going to say.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They know and understand why we have to set out the facts, because Uvaraja has made serious allegations, and it is in the public interests that these allegations are dealt with.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In the course of the investigations, witnesses, from current to ex-officers, were interviewed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Past documentation and records were looked at, and the investigations were thorough.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, Uvaraja said that he had been ill-treated and bullied by his superiors and colleagues.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Specifically, he said: one, there was name-calling; two, shredding of his leave form; and three, abusive language used against him.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, on the name-calling, Uvaraja said that racially inappropriate language had been used against him.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Police records show that Uvaraja had made this complaint in 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They found that the officers involved were talking among themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It does not matter whether they were directed at Uvaraja, or they were not directed at Uvaraja.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja’s superiors made that clear to the team, that such language cannot be used, even as a joke.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The officer who made the remark apologised to Uvaraja immediately in front of the whole team.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If he had not apologised, he would have been made to do so, and disciplinary action would have also been taken against him.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja’s superiors continued to monitor the situation to make sure there were no further recurrences.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja was updated of the outcome of the follow-up and his Deputy Commander had offered the option of lodging an official complaint, but Uvaraja decided that there was no need to file a further complaint.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Since the incident, the Police have conducted a review of their policies and there is a framework of approach for these cases.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is to ensure that there is a record of such an incident, that disciplinary action would be taken, and the officer's subsequent behaviour would be closely monitored.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Police will also continue to engage officers, shape culture and engage in frank discussion on such issues around racial slurs or casual racism.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja also alleged that, in 2019, his superior had shredded his leave form and uploaded a video of this action within a chat group.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The context is this: Uvaraja had applied for discretionary time-off; this does not require the submission of a leave form.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja sent this application at the last minute, when other officers’ leave had already been approved.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And it was not the first time that Uvaraja had done this; applying for time-off at the last minute.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On previous occasions, his teammates who were on leave had to be recalled to cover the manpower shortfall.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In this case, when Uvaraja applied at the last minute again, the superior spoke to Uvaraja about him inconveniencing the entire team.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But Uvaraja maintained his request for time off and asked the superior to end that conversation in the personal chat.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The superior then shredded the leave form and uploaded a recording of him doing so, on the team chatgroup.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He said he did this because the form was not required for Uvaraja’s time-off application, which he had already granted in any case, and the form contained personal information and had to be disposed of.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He should not have done that, even though one can understand his unhappiness.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja had raised this matter up the chain of command.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Allegations were also made that different superiors had used abusive language against Uvaraja.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On the contrary, Uvaraja would often directly message or call his various superiors, and they had responded to him professionally.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The third complaint was not made out and he was also notified about that.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja claimed that his complaints against fellow officers vaping within Police compounds had been covered up.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Investigations found that Uvaraja had made a complaint in 2021 to his superiors about officers vaping.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Acting on the information he provided, Uvaraja’s Commander had directed an independent superior from a different unit to conduct a surprise check.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: All the lockers and personal belongings within the Police compound were checked, even though Uvaraja’s complaint was directed only at a few specific officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Throughout this process, the identity of the whistle-blower, in this case Uvaraja, was not disclosed to the independent superior nor the officers concerned.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For context, in a separate incident in January 2023, Uvaraja reported fellow officers smoking within a different Police compound.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, when the complaint is made out, disciplinary action is taken.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When the complaint is not made out, he is told that the complaint is not made out – no cover up.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Third, Uvaraja claimed that he had been unfairly held back in his career and was given unfair performance appraisals.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja was given opportunities to apply for postings, like his colleagues in the Police Land Divisions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When Uvaraja asked to be transferred, his superiors had facilitated and acceded to his requests, wherever possible.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Those who know about the Police Force will know that that is a significant number of postings.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is significantly more than what is normally given.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Two of his transfers were related to his whistleblowing on the alleged smoking offences because Uvaraja felt uncomfortable working with the colleagues against whom he had reported.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On performance appraisals, investigations found that his performance grades were a fair assessment of his work contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He was also awarded the COVID-19 Resilience Medal.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Fourth, Uvaraja alleged that he had been treated like an outcast by his team.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He said that he had invited his team to his wedding, but nobody had showed up.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: His OC had accepted the invitation but was unable to attend, as he had fallen sick on that day, and the OC had apologised to Uvaraja.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja had also informed his Commanding Officer (CO) about the wedding, but did not follow up with an invitation.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Nevertheless, the CO had congratulated Uvaraja in front of his teammates.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, in summary, Police have done a review of the allegations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The findings for this case were also reviewed by AGC.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And I have reviewed the Police and AGC’s findings and assessment myself.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As for the allegations which were true, actions had been taken when he made the complaints and Uvaraja had been told of the steps that had been taken.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: More broadly, moving to the second aspect of my Ministerial Statement, I will set out how the Police had supported Uvaraja.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Investigations showed that Uvaraja was dealing with a number of personal issues.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Some at the time of his passing and some for periods throughout his Police career.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These included health problems as well as family problems.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Throughout his career as a Police Officer, he had frequently applied for medical leave for periods that sometimes ran into several months in a year.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In some of the years, Uvaraja had also applied for no-pay leave to manage his health issues after he had fully used up his paid leave entitlement.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In addition, Uvaraja also seems to have faced psychological stresses and chronic insomnia.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Since 2017, he had attended multiple psychological consultations for his chronic insomnia.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I am setting these out in summary, without details, because it would be preferable not to go into too much detail about an Officer who has passed away.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Second, Uvaraja seems to have had a tense relationship with both his wife and his family of origin, meaning his mother, his parents, his brother and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In April 2023, Uvaraja’s wife called for Police help during an argument in their matrimonial home.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: She had been stopped by Uvaraja from leaving their home.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On 13 July 2023, the Police received multiple calls for assistance from Uvaraja’s parents’ residence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: His brother alleged that Uvaraja had assaulted him over financial matters.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On 14 July 2023, the next day, Uvaraja’s mother lodged a Police report against Uvaraja, saying she feared for her safety.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On the same day, Uvaraja’s sister-in-law called for the Police, because Uvaraja had come to her house to look for Uvaraja’s parents.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There is more background and there are more facts, relating to these events.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We need to say something of the facts, because Members need an understanding of the situation he faced at that time, when he committed suicide, and the stresses he was under.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And I am trying to convey the position to Members without going too much into the disputes he had with his wife, his mother, his brother and his sister-in-law, which led to the Police reports, and some background to the psychological issues he had and was receiving help for.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He had been granted medical leave from duty at that time to rest and recover.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Instead, he left his house on multiple occasions – and that is a disciplinary offence in the Police force.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In fact, he had not only left his house, but he got into an argument with his family of origin at their flat, which led to calls to the Police and Police reports.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Uvaraja had previously been investigated for similar behaviours in 2016 – going out while on medical leave.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At that time, he had left his place of residence while on medical leave to attend a relative’s graduation and he was given a verbal warning.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He had left his uncompleted work unattended and refused to comply when told to return to finish the tasks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He only did so after being told a third time.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Police had allowed Uvaraja to take substantial amounts of time-off over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In some of the years, Uvaraja had used up all his paid leave entitlements.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, he applied for no-pay leave and his requests were approved.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Members may also access this Annex through the MP@SG PARL mobile app.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is the way the Police have supported him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is a very significant level of support in terms of giving him time off.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Beyond this, since 2016, Uvaraja’s superiors had also arranged for counselling and psychological assistance for him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In January 2023, Uvaraja reported that he was experiencing work stress.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On 16 February 2023, Uvaraja reported to a new unit, following his request to be transferred.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On that day, Uvaraja showed signs of being unstable.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was counselled by a para-counsellor on the same day and was later attended to by a psychologist from the Police Psychological Services Department.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: While Uvaraja was at work, his superiors assessed that his performance was generally below average and had provided guidance to him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This took the form of face-to-face engagements, reviews on the plans for him and setting of achievable targets.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, when he was at the Community Policing Unit from 2018 to 2021, various work templates and resources were given to him to help him carry out his job functions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Uvaraja’s passing and his allegations has affected his Police colleagues.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: His fellow officers who had worked with him across various postings and who were aware of his situation felt sad that he had taken his life.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But they were also disappointed with the untrue claims and allegations that he had made against the Police force.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One officer who had partnered Uvaraja shared that she had encouraged him to start afresh when he was given a new posting, despite his past unhappiness.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: However, she was disappointed that he frequently did not show up for work.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Another officer recalled how he had put in effort to arrange one-on-one chats and meals with Uvaraja and sent well-wishes to him on his birthday to motivate him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have only mentioned two officers, but there were several others, who have helped him during his period in the SPF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They tried their best to help him and their best to care for him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They covered his shifts when he was absent from duties, sometimes even when they had made prior leave plans.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, it is fair to say that many officers pulled together to help him, and they were sad to see a colleague pass away in these circumstances.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But there is also a considerable feeling among the many officers who helped him that, despite so much being done for him by them in their individual capacities, and by SPF as an organisation – because SPF went to considerable lengths to accommodate his needs, including his leave and medical needs – he seems to have externalised many of his issues onto his colleagues in the SPF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For the third aspect of my Ministerial Statement, I will now describe the Home Team’s framework to deal with workplace harassment and grievances.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We had answered Parliamentary Questions (PQs) on this issue last September as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There can be no tolerance for any form of harassment or discrimination in the SPF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The responsibility starts at the top; from me down through the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) management, to the respective agencies’ leadership and then the ranks below.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A core pillar of the framework is training.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: During induction and training of new staff, from the junior ranks to senior officer levels, officers are trained on SPF’s code of ethics, workplace harassment and the actions to be taken if they are victims or witnesses.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Supervisors are also specifically trained on ways to create a harassment-free workplace and support victims of workplace harassment.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In terms of investigating allegations, every functional unit in SPF has a discipline committee headed by the Commander or Director.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In terms of how they function, these discipline committees can convene formal inquiries on their own, or they can refer issues to the Internal Affairs Office (IAO) for further review.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The IAO reports to the Deputy Commissioner of Police and is directly accountable to the Commissioner of Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: All cases of sexual harassment and serious workplace harassment are referred to the IAO for investigations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If wrongdoing is uncovered, the Police, or in appropriate cases, the Public Service Commission, will take disciplinary action.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If criminal offences are disclosed, the Police will recommend prosecution.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Courts take into account the officer’s duty to uphold the law, so the punishment that a Police officer faces is usually more severe than what any other defendant in the Courts or any member of the public can expect to face.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Nine of these were reported to the Public Service Division and Ministry headquarters.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I will now give two examples from the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The second example: in 2020, a Station Inspector (SI) attending a course made sexually insulting and offensive remarks against, or in respect of, his fellow trainees.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The vast majority of our officers hold themselves to a very high standard of conduct, and we cannot allow a small minority who do wrong to colour the public perception of the rest of the force.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And coming to racial insults, of the 310 cases, six complaints were on racial discrimination.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the ground, the Ministry conducts six-monthly Pulse surveys, biennial Public Service Employee Engagement Surveys and triennial 360° surveys of supervisors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: These are all avenues where officers can also provide anonymous comments and feedback, including on workplace issues, so that the Ministry has a good idea of how officers are perceiving issues and what the feelings are on the ground.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our officers have access to a range of support, such as (a) MHA's in-house psychological services; (b) peer support programmes where fellow officers are trained as para-counsellors; (c) a 24/7 helpline managed in-house by our psychologists and para-counsellors; as well as (d) external agency-administered services.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Officers can go and get these measures without needing to report that they have done so, so that it preserves confidentiality.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Officers also attend workshops and courses on how to cope and adapt when dealing with operational and work stresses, and they are sensitised to common mental health issues, such as depression, anxiety, suicide and the helplines that are available.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In October of every year, the Home Team Psychological Services community organises a month-long campaign.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The aim of the campaign is to build awareness of the importance of mental health, the importance of self-care and where to seek help when needed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This approach and culture have been in place for some years now.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And we regularly review and update them to try to ensure that our programmes continue to be relevant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Policing is not easy, and it is not getting easier, either in Singapore or around the world.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In the UK, a survey by the Police Federation of England released last year showed that 87% of police officers said that morale was either low or very low, seven in 10 said that they would not recommend others to join the police force, while 95% said that their morale was harmed by the treatment by their own Government.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In the US, Gallup found, in 2022, that public confidence in the police was just 45%.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The US Department of Justice said in October last year that law enforcement agencies across the US are facing an “historic crisis in recruiting and retaining qualified candidates”.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police forces around the world are facing increasing challenges for many reasons.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some of them are: first, there is a trend of laws in other countries being progressively weakened against law enforcement, making it more difficult for the police to arrest, more difficult to investigate and more difficult for the state to prosecute and get convictions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is easier for people to commit crimes due to laxer laws and it is easier for those who have committed crimes to walk away.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The mentality is often one of the “individual versus the system”, where the system – the law enforcement institutions – are usually painted out to be the villains.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Officers feel like the situation is stacked against them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And this is compounded by a second reason.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Around the world, many police forces are struggling to pay their officers adequately.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If conditions of service are not good, it will be difficult to attract and retain good people for this tough job.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Third, some police forces are also struggling with corruption in their system.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This arises due to many factors – poor discipline, low morale and poor leadership, among others.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have to guard against all of these developing in Singapore and to make sure that SPF continues to retain the trust of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, a few months ago, in October last year, Police Commanding Officer, Superintendent Lim, was convicted after being charged in Court.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was caught drink-driving at a Police roadblock.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In many countries, I dare say, these offences by police officers which were picked up by other police officers would have never seen the light of day.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A police officer who drinks and drives and is caught at a police roadblock, he will not be charged.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But in Singapore, he will be, because the Police force takes a very serious view of errant Police officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Members might also be aware of the case involving Staff Sergeant Kevin Chelvam, who allegedly stood by while his domestic helper was abused by his family members.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was charged for abetting his wife in starving the domestic helper, causing hurt to the helper, removing evidence and lying to the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When we come across these situations, action is taken, and it is dealt with publicly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But as I said, these are the exceptions, a very small number of exceptions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The vast majority of our officers are honest.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They have strong ethos, strong esprit de corps and integrity.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I said in May last year at the Police Workplan Seminar: “Our officers know that when there are false or unfair allegations, we will act quickly and decisively to tell the truth and stand by the officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that starts with me and the Permanent Secretary and the entire Police leadership.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State Assoc Prof Dr Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We take seriously all allegations of such nature and will investigate them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have put in place various safeguards to deter and detect such behaviours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This was covered in Minister Shanmugam’s written reply to Parliamentary Questions (PQs) on avenues for Home Team officers to raise complaints in September last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will highlight some of the key points from that reply and make further elaborations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But first, let me summarise the outcome of the investigations into the late Sgt Uvaraja’s allegations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Where the complaints were substantiated, appropriate actions had already been taken, and errant officers had already been taken to task.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As for the reporting channels available for Home Team officers to raise grievances or report wrongdoing or workplace discrimination, they can do so to any level of management through the Channel for Formal Grievance Handling and the Channel for Confidential Ethical Disclosure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Officers are informed of these reporting channels when they first join MHA and at various engagement sessions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are clear escalation guidelines and processes to ensure that all reports of workplace discrimination, unfair treatment, or misconduct are investigated objectively, professionally and expeditiously.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Officers who are not satisfied with the outcome of an investigation can further escalate the matter up within the Ministry, the Public Service Division (PSD), or even to the Head of Civil Service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Officers can also provide anonymous feedback, including on workplace discrimination issues, through MHA’s Pulse Surveys, Public Service Employee Engagement Surveys, and 360° Surveys of supervisors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Feedback received through these surveys are taken seriously and investigated where necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: And of the 50, three were for racial discrimination, two of which were from the Police force.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These formal organisational reporting channels are necessary but insufficient on their own.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Every officer has a role to play in ensuring that the workplace remains safe for everyone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Officers can attend programmes and trainings to learn about cultural, religious and racial sensitivities and about behaviours that constitute bullying and sexual harassment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Through such trainings, we empower officers with the skills to detect and deter workplace harassment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: At the same time, we assure them that they can come forward when they witness or become victims of workplace harassment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, Minister Shanmugam, Second Minister Josephine Teo, Minister of State Sun Xueling and I, as well as the Home Team senior management, regularly engage our officers in dialogues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We do this to get a better sense of the challenges they face on a day-to-day basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: During these sessions, officers do surface issues and their concerns, and they can also do so anonymously via the online platform which may be set up for the dialogues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In some instances, we arrange for a smaller group session if the officers prefer to speak to us in a more private setting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We take seriously all the issues and concerns that are raised by our officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We treat all such allegations seriously and investigate thoroughly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There have indeed been a few black sheep; no organisation or society can completely eliminate all harassment and discrimination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But such cases remain far and few within the Home Team.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: And if we do find any wrongdoing, rest assured that we will not hesitate to take the culpable officers to task, regardless of seniority.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This is the only way to maintain and keep the confidence and trust of our officers, and the public whom we serve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: (In Mandarin):   Minister Shanmugam has spoken at length on the case and the broader issues of workplace discrimination and mental health support for Home Team officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, MHA's efforts in supporting the mental well-being of our officers; and second, fostering a culture that values and respects diversity at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Where the complaints were substantiated, appropriate actions had already been taken at that time, and errant officers had already been taken to task.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Mental health struggles can affect us all, regardless of age, gender or profession.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The pandemic had exacerbated some of the stressors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The key initiatives include training employees to support and care for their colleagues' mental well-being, training supervisors to recognise common mental health conditions and offering mental wellness programmes to equip employers and employees with the skills and knowledge to better take charge of their mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the Home Team, the mental health and well-being of our officers are of utmost importance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As shared in Parliament in October 2022, our Home Team officers are provided with various forms of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These include MHA's in-house psychological services and peer support programmes comprising officers trained as para-counsellors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is a 24/7 helpline managed in-house by our psychologists and para-counsellors, as well as external agency-administered services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are also organisational level initiatives to raise awareness and educate officers on the importance of mental health and how to deal with stressors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, we will organise resilience building workshops for newly joined officers and awareness programmes to learn the ways to cope and adapt when dealing with operational and work stresses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are also courses to train supervisors on how to support their officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are communication initiatives to raise officers' literacy on common mental health issues, such as depression, anxiety and suicide, and inform them of the various helplines available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In October every year, the Home Team Psychological Services community organises a month-long campaign to remind officers on the importance of self-care and where to seek help when needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our programmes are regularly reviewed to ensure relevancy and are updated with new developments and interventions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We value and respect the richness such diversity brings and recognise that maintaining a harmonious workplace in the face of such diversity cannot be taken for granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We put in effort to build trust and acceptance, embrace differences and proactively deal with any bias or racism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In supervisory workshops, sensitivity to and respect of various cultures and races are discussed and reinforced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MHA officers at all levels are reminded of the importance of cultivating a harassment-free workplace and how they should support victims of workplace harassment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are also team cohesion programmes for officers to bond and get to know each other better.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Home Team Departments also organise celebrations of the various festivals of every race.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These celebrations reinforce our appreciation of the differences among us, promote inclusiveness and enhance our understanding of each other's culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In a multiracial society, everyone plays a part in building a culture of respect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The majority must be sensitive to the concerns of the minority and be mindful of our actions and words.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The minority must not allow suspicion to colour how we perceive every action and word of the majority.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They must necessarily rely on and count on each other to be successful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We therefore put strong emphasis on team leaders building strong bonds within their teams and ensuring that the officers value and respect the diversity in the Home Team.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before I call Members to ask for clarifications if they have any, I wish to remind Members that pursuant to Standing Order 23, Members may seek clarification on the Ministerial Statement, but there is no debate that should be allowed thereon.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members can seek clarifications by way of asking questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I seek Members' understanding to keep your clarifications clear and concise.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Likewise, I would like to ask the Ministers to also keep your answers clear and concise.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My questions pertain to what the public came to know about the suicide involving Sgt Uvaraja and, naturally, you have different perspectives out there, and, to the extent that the Minister could, I think the clarifications he provided in the House were helpful.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, there is also a post by an individual who was the senior counsellor of the late Sgt Uvaraja.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think there were some allegations that he made as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Minister responded in his statement to Sgt Uvaraja's allegations, but I would just like to confirm whether the allegations by the senior counsellor have also been looked into.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think there were comments regarding the sheer abuse of authority and the fact that the late Sgt Uvaraja endured prolonged surveillance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, for completeness, can the Minister also confirm the veracity of these allegations, as I think this post still remains online?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second clarification is with regard to, again, the post of the senior counsellor who said that he referred Sgt Uvaraja to the Police Psychological Services Division.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can the Minister share what is the usual procedure for such referrals?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the second question as to what happens when a matter is referred to a psychological team, I covered that in my Statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In this case, he was referred to a para-counsellor, for example, last year, and then to a Police counsellor.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I forgot the exact specification; it is in my Statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How much further it needs to go and how long it needs to go is fact specific.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are also external agencies that the Police can tap on too.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The kind of support that will be given and the very extensive structure of support available will be fact specific and will depend on what the officer needs.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I did not take down the third point.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, I will go to the fourth point.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On morale in the Police force, what I can say is, let me give a few statistics off the top of my head and give a broader perspective.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You do not get those figures in other countries and there is a reason.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The reason is, among other things, with yesterday's passing of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC), the Police know that we will give the appropriate powers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police know I will stand up here and make a Ministerial Statement defending the Police when they have done no wrong.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will also charge our Police officers when they have done wrong in public.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, even though a Superintendent, a senior Police officer, is caught by another Police officer at a roadblock drunk driving, he will be charged.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is why we have transparency; they know we have transparency; that is why we have trust.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We do not make the Police the subject of political football.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And we do not make the Police the scapegoats every time there are inconvenient questions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We come out; we tell the truth; we defend them where they ought to be defended.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member could tell me what the third question is, I will deal with that, too.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Sorry, I did not answer the Member's question on morale.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is strong esprit de corps and strong morale, because they know that this Government does the right thing by them and this Government has always done the right thing.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They know that people cannot just make allegations against the Police force.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member wants precise numbers, I can give them to the Member if he could put in a PQ.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just to reply to the Minister, I had three questions, not four.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Whenever a complaint or an allegation is brought up and involves an internal matter, I think it is often more painful and more difficult when it comes from an external source because this leads to great stress, anxiety and awkwardness for the person making the complaint.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And indeed, for those who then have to be investigated and who then have to be questioned, it can also be an uncomfortable time as well, and that could affect not just the morale but the teamwork and the esprit de corps within the team.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, I wanted to just ask the Minister if he could share whether there are measures taken to help deal with the mental and emotional stress that perhaps officers who are being investigated or being questioned are facing as a result of the complaint, such that they are able to deal with that difficult period of questioning and even after the matter has been closed as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One, there has to be a proper and thorough investigation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that, in itself, I accept can be stressful and will often be stressful, but we have no choice.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And the officer will know that if he has done nothing wrong, the investigations will clear him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Equally, he will know that if the allegations against him are likely to be made out, then, of course, I can understand that that would add to the stress.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The situation does not mean that the officer is precluded from seeking psychological assistance that I spoke about.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He can continue to avail himself of the help, speak with his counsellors and receive such psychological support as necessary because he continues to be a member of the Police force.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Having regard to a situation where there is a Police officer who has not been performing for quite an extended period of time – not attending work and also has psychological problems – and the natural tendency of Police officers to want to help their colleagues, how do we balance that against public interest, having regard to the fact that the Police officer has solemn duties and is also armed when he is on duty as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: How do we make sure that a decision in relation to his employment is made ultimately in the public interest and, hopefully, also to protect him in the long run?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is the question about how do we make sure he is in employment, meaning how do we make sure that he remains in employment or how do we make sure that he does not remain in employment?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The question I have is in relation to how do we make sure a decision is made in public interest for a person who is seen not to be able to function for an extended period of time?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And drawing from this case, there are psychological issues, so how do we make a decision in the public interest to even consider termination of the person's employment?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Assessment of the Police officers' performance has to be made over a period of time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: His performance grades will have to be looked at over that period of time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Subjectively, in terms of how people will help, at least speaking for the Police force and from this case, Members will know that if a person is not performing, his colleagues do come around him to try and support, which they have tried to do even at the expense of their own leave arrangements; they have tried to rally around him and support him to try and get him to perform better.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The third aspect to the question is: if allegations are made and investigations are conducted, those have to be professional and independent.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A different department, or CID, will conduct the investigations where, quite often, you can be sure that the Police will do that robustly without consideration of the fact that the person is a Police officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, the fact that he is a Police officer often counts against the person in Court if, indeed, he is charged.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is no reason to doubt the findings.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I also agree with the Minister that we have to look after the morale of the Police force.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, in this case, a Police officer has taken his own life after alleging workplace bullying, racial discrimination and unfair treatment after whistleblowing within the SPF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think the Member perhaps did not listen to my Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am not sure if he was in the Chamber when I talked about the UK.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then the Member would have heard me saying what the morale of the UK police officers was.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think the Member would recall more than half, a significant number, take a very dim view of their prospects; 70% will not recommend somebody else to join the force and a significant number blamed their own government and the endless inquiries.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Every time there is an allegation, there is a committee of inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Every time there is an allegation, they are made the subject of being scapegoated.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you put officers through this each time there is an allegation, that is, public inquiries, what are you really saying?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That they will be put out there and hung out to dry regardless of the facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You ask yourself: do you think more people are going to join the Police force?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is that the kind of society we want?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The bottom line is, do we trust the Police force?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Why do you think 90% of Singaporeans have trust in the Police force?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Why do we take a theoretical approach when, in practice, in Singapore, it is a low-crime society, and it is a high trust society; there is tremendous trust in the Police force?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We solve crimes with the methods that we have used.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, what is it about those methods that are wrong?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Why do you want to go down a route like the UK has?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Have you seen the results of their system?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Yesterday I set out what happens in other countries; and today, I went back to talking about what happens in other countries.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If there is something specific that the Member, Mr Leong, has in terms of the facts that have been disclosed, dpes the Member question the form that I set out on the medical leave and the no-pay leave of the officer?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Does the Member question the point that I made that he made three allegations of bullying?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, when the Member talks about a Committee of Inquiry or Commission of Inquiry, I would invite the Member to say which part of this explanation does he disagree with or finds questionable?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Perhaps, if the Member would illuminate that and explain that, then we can discuss, rather than, in generalities, that we ought to follow other systems when our system is doing much better than any of these systems that the Member can refer to.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Perhaps the Member can tell me which part of the explanation he thinks is questionable.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I said there is no reason to doubt the finding.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think people know why I raised the question, because justice must not only be done, it must also be seen to be done.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In this case, we are not asking for – or at least I am not asking for – that, in the future, any complaints about our Police force, we will make a big fuss out of it.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But in this case, I am saying it is very special, well, unfortunately, it is very special, because a Policeman has given up his life.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, I thought we should investigate this case with a Committee of Inquiry.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But, of course, we respect the decisions made by the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I am just asking the Minister what has been, in his mind, when he made the decision?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is a matter of considerable regret to me personally, and I am sure to every Member in this House, that someone took his life.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In particular, it is a matter of considerable regret and dismay for the Home Team, that he is a Police officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It affects me, it affects the Police force and his colleagues.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: None of us wants to see it and we have the deepest of feelings for his family and for himself.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that is why I have taken considerable care not to go into what exactly happened, except to set out in the briefest of outlines.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Regret is even not adequate to convey the very deep feelings we have about what happened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, it is 80 days where he was at work, minus weekends or days off.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, again, that level of flexibility was given.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is a caring organisation that cared for him and gave him a lot of support.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then, come back to 2022, he was on no-pay leave for about 160 days, and he was on medical leave for 80 days – that is 240 days out of 360, excluding weekends.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not think you will see this in many organisations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Certainly, not in the private sector, but the Police force had been very, very supportive of trying to help this officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that is the approach they take to every Police officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Any Police officer taking his life is a tragedy for us.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And likewise, any allegation, whether by a Police officer or not, has to be taken seriously, as I explained why.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And when it is by a Police officer, it will be taken seriously by the public; and the Police will, of course, also take it seriously, simply because a Police officer making these allegations can be expected to know more about what he is saying in context.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are proper cases for a Committee of Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are proper cases for a Commission of Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have explained when some matters will go for Committee of Inquiry and Commission for Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is a matter where I have set out the facts publicly and people can assess for themselves how the facts look.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day and Notices of Motion.
